gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-sundan: Relaxed and a bit loose, Fuzzy Bubbles draws rounded letters with a drafting pen's unwavering line, while Noto Sans Sundanese stays plain sans and tidy. Handwriting meets order, and neither crowds the other.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-syloti: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri has short ascenders, a tall x-height and an a whose lower bowl opens up. Fuzzy Bubbles then adds a bent-paperclip handwritten look with no swelling, so the sans text feels friendlier beside it.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Soft, hand-drawn and a little goofy. Fuzzy Bubbles keeps one unit-width stroke throughout, and Noto Sans Syriac sits beneath it with bulb-like lowercase bowls and s shapes that turn wide and easy.

Hand-sketched, friendly and wiry. If Fuzzy Bubbles were made small, its monoline strokes would crowd together, whereas Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps its tall lowercase and far-apart curve endings clear even when it runs large.
Doodled, rounded and relaxed, Fuzzy Bubbles holds every line at a constant thickness against the sturdy, bundled-cable lowercase of Noto Sans Syriac Western. Loose handwriting, firm text.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-tagalo: Fuzzy Bubbles looks sketched in pencil that never presses harder, with small letters nearly as tall as its capitals. Noto Sans Tagalog does the opposite job, filling the middle of each line with generous curve gaps.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-tagban: Relaxed, with letters that look bent from a single wire. Fuzzy Bubbles leads with its personal handwriting, and Noto Sans Tagbanwa follows in sans-serif, its open curves and tall lowercase keeping the text easy to take in.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Fuzzy Bubbles is handwritten yet strokes never shift from heavy to light, each line looking drawn with a drafting pen in a relaxed hand. Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its ink strokes out softly beside it.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-tai-th: Noto Sans Tai Tham crowds its chalk-board lowercase up toward the capital line, with open c shapes you can see into. Fuzzy Bubbles, meanwhile, is the warmer one, with rounded handwriting and no hairlines at all.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-tai-vi: Noto Sans Tai Viet reads crisp and approachable, with short ascenders, a tall x-height and terminals pulled back from its curves. Fuzzy Bubbles brings the handwritten warmth, its t sharing one width in crossbar and stem.
